Subject: Hosted API — transient tokenization congestion (status RDW-5632)

Jessica — quick heads-up: we observed a transient congestion event in our tokenization pipeline that affected some hosted generation endpoints beginning ~08:53 PDT. You may see elevated p95/p99 latencies and, in a narrow set of requests, partial generation stalls (some requests retried by our routing). We’ve posted an incident on the status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RDW-5632

Impact summary:
- Window: ~08:53–09:40 PDT (mitigation started at 09:20, full rollback by 09:40)
- Symptoms: elevated p95 for generative endpoints (up to 2.5x), small fraction (~0.6%) of 503/partial responses, queueing symptoms on tokenization workers
- Scope: hosted inference region us-west1; NovaSol’s production traffic may have seen increased latency and intermittent partial responses

Actions we took:
- Shifted routing away from affected worker pool (09:10)
- Applied emergency rollback of tokenizer runtime change (09:20)
- Increased temporary batching thresholds and drained token-queue backlog (09:25–09:40)
- Posted incident details to status page and opened a post-incident doc (attached)

Next steps for you: I wanted to surface the incident proactively and share the summary (attached). We’ll follow up with a short postmortem with root cause and mitigations by EOD. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute sync with engineering to walk the technical details.

Apologies for the disruption — we know latency is critical for NovaSol. I’m copying our CS/ops leads and will share the formal postmortem when ready.

— Karthik

Karthik — quick update from SRE/Runtime: root cause identified as a tokenizer buffer regression introduced in runtime 2.8.1 (edge case with short-sequence batching). We rolled back the runtime on the affected worker pool at 09:20 and drained the backlog by 09:40; system telemetry indicates service metrics returned to baseline by 09:45.

We have prepared an internal postmortem draft and a customer-friendly one-pager (attached to this thread). For NovaSol-level remediation, I suggest the following:
- Credit: one week pro-rated credit on March consumption (suggested draft: 15% for impacted window)
- Postmortem: share a 1-page timeline + root cause + permanent mitigation ETA (we’ve scheduled a follow-up patch for runtime 2.8.2 with improved buffer checks)
- Optional: 30-minute technical review with our runtime engineer (we can schedule for tomorrow)

Grace — confirm the credit recommendation and the patch ETA; Jessica — please let us know whether a call tomorrow morning works or if you prefer written follow-up.
